prompt: In three sentences, explain why the sky is blue.
content: The sky is blue because of Rayleigh scattering: sunlight is made up of all colors, and when it enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules much smaller than light's wavelength. This scattering affects shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) far more than longer ones (red and orange), so blue light is dispersed in all directions across the sky. Although violet light scatters even more, the sun emits less of it, our eyes are less sensitive to it, and some is absorbed in the upper atmosphere—so we perceive the sky as blue.
